assertion: As of the end of 2025, there were 75 active drug shortages in the U.S., with only 4 of those 75 first reported in 2025 (nearly all carried over from 2024).
article_value: 75 active shortages; 4 of 75 first reported in 2025
warehouse_value: 75 distinct generic_name with status='Current'; 4 of those with initial_posting_date in 2025
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT generic_name) FROM health.fda_drug_shortages_history WHERE snapshot_date='2025-12-16' AND status='Current'; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT generic_name) FROM health.fda_drug_shortages_history WHERE snapshot_date='2025-12-16' AND status='Current' AND initial_posting_date LIKE '%2025'

sources.title: USP Annual Drug Shortages Report finds rising discontinuations, hidden upstream risk (USP press release, republished by BioSpace)

reason: Independent reconstruction of FDA's own drug shortage list matches USP's headline figures exactly.

assertion: Product discontinuations rose 60% from 2024 to 2025 (the largest single-year increase since 2019), and sterile injectable drugs make up 71% of all active shortages, the largest share of any dosage form.
article_value: 60% YoY discontinuation increase; 71% of shortages are sterile injectables
warehouse_value: 55.4% YoY discontinuation increase (112 to 174 distinct drugs); 69.3% of current shortages (52 of 75) have an injectable presentation
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT generic_name) FROM health.fda_drug_shortages_history WHERE snapshot_date='2025-01-17' AND discontinued_date LIKE '%/2024'; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT generic_name) FROM health.fda_drug_shortages_history WHERE snapshot_date='2026-01-20' AND discontinued_date LIKE '%/2025'; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT generic_name), COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN presentation ILIKE '%Injection%' OR presentation ILIKE '%Injectable%' THEN generic_name END) FROM health.fda_drug_shortages_history WHERE snapshot_date='2025-12-16' AND status='Current'

sources.title: Report: How Drug Discontinuations Surged Despite Shortage Numbers Declining (Pharmaceutical Commerce, citing USP's report directly)

reason: Same direction and close magnitude; small numeric gap likely reflects USP counting discontinuation events/NDCs and a stricter sterile-injectable classification rather than distinct-generic-name text matching used here.
